KR.read: No processed DataPoints exist for men's grooming in South Korea (data/processed/KR_mens_grooming.json is absent, and the pre-shaped segment file shows size, growth, cagr, and export all null). There is nothing in the system to read for this geography x segment at present.
KR.trend: Growth direction cannot be assessed from current data.
KR.caveats: This is a data gap, not a finding of zero or flat market activity — no fetch or manual drop has populated this segment for Korea yet.

IN.read: The HIGH-confidence figure, Euromonitor International's RETAIL-basis market size, puts India men's grooming at INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) for 2025. Separately, IMARC estimates (LOW confidence) put a narrower 'male grooming products' basket at US$2.3bn (2024) rising to US$2.45bn (2025). These two size estimates use the same RETAIL value_basis but differ in scope (whole segment vs a narrower product basket), so they should not be read as confirming or contradicting one another.
IN.trend: Observed growth is +9.0% YoY for 2025 (HIGH confidence, Euromonitor, RETAIL basis). A cagr_forecast of 12.2% (2025-2035, LOW confidence, Future Market Insights) is a forecast, not an observed trend, and it explicitly covers the men's SKINCARE sub-slice rather than the whole men's grooming segment, so it should not be read as this segment's overall forecast growth rate.
IN.caveats: Confidence is uneven across the underlying figures: the single HIGH-confidence data point (Euromonitor size and growth) sits alongside several LOW-confidence aggregator figures (IMARC, Future Market Insights) that also vary in scope (narrower 'male grooming products' basket, or a men's-skincare-only sub-slice for the 12.2% CAGR).

combined.read: A side-by-side KR vs IN comparison is not possible for this segment: Korea has no processed DataPoints at all for men's grooming, so there is no value_usd_bn (or any other figure) to set against India's US$1.94bn (2025, HIGH confidence, RETAIL). config/corridor.yaml separately lists 'Men's K-beauty' as a corridor whitespace opportunity (baseline whitespace #4, describing men's skincare as underserved relative to toiletries), but this is a qualitative whitespace note in the corridor registry, not a quantified [CORRIDOR]-tagged DataPoint within this segment's files, and none of the India DataPoints read here carry a [CORRIDOR] tag.
